executiveSummary: GM0168 passes the complete deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, generalized boundary, 23,469 residents, 13 neighbourhoods, five BAG places, eight BRT settlement labels and Twente safety-region assignment reconcile. Release nevertheless remains correction-required. Nine non-earthquake hazard families reuse one complete neighbourhood ranking at T+24, and a controlled wildfire source inside Verspreide huizen Beuningen ranks only sixth of thirteen. The named Rhine, Meuse & IJssel preset produces a precise nonzero local river severity and service trajectory although Veiligheidsregio Twente says this high sandy municipality has no primary dike rings and identifies the distinct cross-border Dinkel/Regge rainfall pathway instead. Losser's six Dutch logical routes contain no German node, omit the N731 Glane-Gronau and A1/Germany continuities, and reuse roads for every service. Current public-context zeros for weather, warnings, seismic events, roads, acute care, PM2.5 and Waterinfo are NoData/coverage results, never evidence of safety. Public authoritative Dinkel, upstream German gauge, Overijssel pluvial, water-asset, forest, grid-planning and external-care sources can improve typed context, but no public safe source establishes live utility topology, facility acceptance, household supplies, operational actions or restoration through 72 hours. Those states must remain Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

evidenceSources.title: Gemeente and buurt gegeneraliseerd 2025 with BAG, BRT TOP10NL, NWB and railway context

BAG woonplaatsen are accessible under Public Domain Mark 1.0 at https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/bag/ogc/v2/collections/woonplaats. BRT TOP10NL is CC BY 4.0 at https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-top10nl/ogc/v1 with rotating updates and supplies eight settlement labels and source-scale topography.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Twente 2025 and first-72-hour preparedness guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile 2025, adopted 23 April 2026 and published 2 June 2026; guidance inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Twente is relatively high and has no dike rings or primary flood defences. The cross-border Dinkel and Regge can produce locally limited, short-lived flooding after prolonged or intense regional or German rainfall; river levels may rise days later. This differs from Rhine, Meuse & IJssel high water.

High sandy terrain makes local water supply rainfall-dependent and susceptible to drought. Nature areas combine recreation, campsites and care with constrained access, limited extinguishing water and setup time for large water transport.

Losser's five villages lie against the German border. The profile requires cross-border crisis cooperation across differing language, culture and law and retains residual Emsland/Lingen radiological coordination context after the plant's 2023 shutdown.

Power-loss planning distinguishes 0–2, 2–8, over 8 and over 24 hour phases, and drinking-water planning separates quantity from bacteriological and chemical quality. The September 2021 multi-day boil advisory around Losser/Oldenzaal is historical mechanism evidence, not a current incident state or a restoration promise.

Twente Veilig guidance at https://twenteveilig.nl/zorg-voor-een-noodpakket recommends supplies for 72 hours and three litres of water per person per day. It is guidance, not measured preparedness. No blanket reuse licence was established for the risk-profile PDF.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Vechtstromen / Niedersächsischer Landesbetrieb für Wasserwirtschaft, Küsten- und Naturschutz
evidenceSources.title: Dinkeldal, Dinkel-Zuid, Glanerbeek and upstream Lage I Dinkel gauge context
evidenceSources.edition: Public project and current-condition pages plus German gauge service inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The Dinkel originates just across the border between Coesfeld and Ahaus, enters Twente near Gronau, crosses the Netherlands and Germany and reaches the Vecht near Neuenhaus. Municipality clipping cannot represent its source-to-receptor system.

Dinkel-Zuid runs from the German border through Weertsbrug in Glane and Zoekerbrug south of Losser to Ellermansbrug in the N731. Current works seek temporary retention for downstream flood and drought buffering; completed or planned works are not proof of event-time protection or capacity.

The 4.5 km Glanerbeek crosses Germany and has been adapted for temporary storage under extreme weather with Gronau, Kreis Borken and German water bodies. A completed project is mechanism/context, not a live state or T+72 guarantee.

NLWKN Lage I at https://www.pegelonline.nlwkn.niedersachsen.de/Pegel/Karte/Binnenpegel/ID/388 exposes timestamped Dinkel measurements through a documented REST service, generally hourly from 15-minute means with possible gaps or unverified values. It is an upstream observation/replay input, not an inundation surface or forecast; exact reuse terms require review.

Vechtstromen's 26 August 2026 drought update ended specified temporary restrictions from 27 August while retaining the regular abstraction rule tied to flow past the first downstream weir. This is authority lifecycle context, not a measured Losser-wide water state.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RIVM / RDI / DUO / NDW / Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: Public water assets, grid planning, acute care, telecom, education, roads and environmental context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployed/public services inspected 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care questionnaire 2026 v1.1
supports: The deployed HWH snapshot intersects 165 features: 158 weirs, three sewer pumps, three surface-water pumps and one wastewater-treatment feature; 161 name Vechtstromen as manager and four are null. Rioolgemaal De Lutte, Rioolgemaal Glane and RWZI Losser have null capacity/status/manager in the snapshot. HWH is CC BY-SA 4.0, partial and contributor-dependent; object presence is not hydraulic connectivity or live operation.

Netbeheer Nederland public planning JSON for postcode 7587AL reports service area LS Losser/Enexis, withdrawal existing/required/queued 41/21/1.5 MW with ten queued requests, injection 41/42.8/30.7 MW with eight queued requests, and twelve projects with earliest year 2026. It is one postcode's planning context, not municipality coverage, live topology, load, outage or restoration; exact API licence/stability are unstated.

RIVM's versioned CC0 2026 v1.1 questionnaire lists no acute-hospital point inside GM0168. External 24/7 acute care includes Medisch Spectrum Twente in Enschede and ZGT Almelo; reported roles, room counts and 2025 visits do not establish incident-time travel, staffing, occupancy, acceptance, power/fuel or diversion.

The deployed context contains 55 RDI sites and 15 DUO locations. Antenna and education records do not establish coverage, backhaul, backup, shelter, care or distribution roles. Public-context assignment returns zero GM0168 records for government service, KNMI observation/warning/seismic, NDW road situations, RIVM acute care/PM2.5 and RWS Waterinfo; every zero is NoData/coverage, not safety or absence.

Publishers, versions, retrieval and validity times, coverage, licence and evidence class differ across these sources. Static registers, timestamped observations, forecasts, official scenarios and synthetic model values must remain separate and non-causal unless an explicit adapter contract says otherwise.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared neighbourhood seed and failed local fire-source containment cannot represent Losser's hazard-specific geography.
notes: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial flood, named river, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack and canonical wildfire have exactly the same full 13-neighbourhood order; compound only swaps the first two and repeats the common order at T+72. Earthquake is a zero-hazard baseline order.

Verspreide huizen Glane, Bedrijfsterrein Losser, Verspreide huizen De Lutte, Glane-Beekhoek and Glane kern lead the reused order; Losser-Oost, Overdinkel kern, Losser-West, De Lutte kern and Verspreide huizen Overdinkel trail. No local source surface for any mechanism drives this rank.

No Dinkel footprint, 70 mm/2 h province raster, valid-time weather field, named cyber target or selected seismic ground-motion grid controls local allocation.

At T+72 most deteriorate further to 0.309543, 0.290546, 0.211739, 0.515311, 0.225165, 0.823017, 0.279116 and 0.857269 without cited operational evidence.

Provider/planning areas, HWH objects, antenna sites, hospitals and schools are non-causal context. They do not establish feeder, pipe, sewer, backhaul or patient-transfer connectivity, live capacity/state, priority, backup, stock, crew or repair path.
Drinking-water quantity/pressure and bacteriological/chemical quality, wastewater collection/treatment and regional surface-water control must remain distinct systems.

causalTrace.summary: Stage arithmetic closes, but generic major-river forcing, shared spatial allocation and cross-border omissions make the local causal story physically unsupported.
notes: The named Rhine, Meuse & IJssel preset holds GM0168 severity at 0.137479541 and normalized flood stress at 0.442158366 through T+24/T+72; affected grows 1,186 to 1,551 and cumulative person-hours 67,777.157 to 278,416.486. Seven services remain exactly fixed while facilities alone changes from 0.820417 to 0.741606.

E03 says Twente has no primary dike rings and E04 identifies Dinkel/German-rain mechanisms. The generic nonzero direct major-river path therefore has no cited local forcing, depth, arrival/recession, control state or NoData mask.

Coastal T+24 has zero direct flood and zero affected with severity 0.021214, correctly narrow for marine forcing, but it cannot mean all-clear for Dinkel, pluvial, wind, transport or cross-border supply effects.
Static registers, current observations, official scenarios, historical incidents and synthetic outputs remain separate evidence classes; none may be silently projected through 72 hours.

recovery72h.summary: The 72-hour curves are deterministic but not calibrated to cross-border hydrology, forest fire, operators, routes, facilities, supplies or action completion.
notes: Storm, pluvial, winter and cyber have zero direct local forcing at T+72 while cumulative person-hours continue to 302,854.761, 260,772.932, 285,714.618 and 395,573.503. That may represent persistence, but no local operator or response plan validates the exact recovery curves.

Heat water availability rises from 0.482247 at T+24 to 0.900779 at T+72 and direct affected rounds to zero; canonical wildfire remains indirect smoke/drought with zero direct fire and zero affected. Neither path uses a selected local event or operational recovery evidence.

Compound severity declines from 0.936524 peak to 0.553442 at T+72 while affected rises to 14,207 and most services worsen from T+24 to T+72. The simulator records no intervention, resource constraint, owner or completion evidence that explains this trajectory.

No selected German/Dinkel hydrograph, KNMI issue/valid time, utility switching, water-quality state, HWH control telemetry, road/bridge condition, hospital acceptance, reception/water point, household stock, crew/fuel/spare allocation or action status drives recovery. Seventy-two hours is a preparedness horizon, not a recovery deadline.

findings.summary: The named major-river preset gives Losser precise direct forcing without local Rhine, Meuse or IJssel evidence while omitting the separate Dinkel pathway.
findings.evidence: The river preset fixes severity at 0.137479541 and normalized flood stress at 0.442158366 through T+72, with 1,551 affected and 278,416.486 cumulative person-hours at T+72. E03 says Twente has no primary dike rings and identifies locally limited Dinkel/Regge flooding after sustained regional/German rain; E04 establishes the cross-border Dinkel/Glanerbeek and an upstream German gauge. No selected hydrograph, depth footprint, threshold, control state, arrival/recession or uncertainty drives the output.
findings.action: Set direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel exposure to evidence-supported zero or unsupported for GM0168, and implement Dinkel/regional-water as a separate typed pathway. Require a water-manager-selected cross-border rainfall/hydrograph, datum, connected footprint or threshold rules, arrival/recession, controls, uncertainty, licence and NoData before nonzero local claims.

findings.summary: Nine hazard families reuse a shared neighbourhood seed rather than mechanism-specific Losser evidence.

findings.action: Replace the shared seed with hazard-specific, coverage-aware surfaces. Preserve source edition, issue/valid time, CRS, resolution, units, scenario, licence and NoData and explicitly mark each unsupported dimension until a selected source exists.

findings.summary: Pluvial depth, drainage, Dinkel receiving water and road/facility thresholds are not connected to the official Overijssel scenario.

findings.summary: The closed Dutch graph omits Losser's German upstream-water, road, care and mutual-aid dependencies.
findings.evidence: All six graph links terminate in Oldenzaal, Enschede or Dinkelland. There is no German node, N731 Glane-Gronau, A1/Germany continuation, upstream Lage I Dinkel dependency or authority/mutual-aid edge. findings.action: Add typed country/authority/direction/mode cross-border edges for water boundary conditions, mobility/logistics, care and mutual aid using authorized Dutch and German sources. Keep mobility distinct from utilities and require valid-time state before operational passability claims.

findings.summary: One road-derived graph cannot establish eight physical lifelines or the exact T+24/T+72 service trajectory.
findings.evidence: Every link lacks supportedServices, so all eight services reuse A1/N-road edges. Compound availability worsens from T+24 to T+72 for most services without an intervention or operator plan. findings.action: Restrict NWB causality to mobility and explicitly assumed logistics/repair access. Require per-service topologySemantics, evidence/version and Unknown fields; use only the smallest transparent aggregate synthetic fallback until security-reviewed operator, water-board, municipality, telecom and GHOR inputs exist.

findings.summary: External acute care, drinking-water quality, village access, household supplies and first-72-hour actions are absent from the causal timeline.
findings.evidence: GM0168 has no RIVM acute-hospital point; external MST and ZGT records do not establish incident-time reachability or acceptance. The regional profile separates drinking-water quantity from quality and records a historical multi-day boil advisory. The model has no facility status, shelter/water point, road/bridge state, household stock, owner, task, resource, action status or completion evidence. Official 72-hour guidance is not measured readiness.
findings.action: Model route-dependent care access separately from facility capability and water quantity separately from quality. Add an auditable proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled action ledger with owner, source, issue/valid time, expiry, resource constraint and confidence; keep every unconfirmed action or stock Unknown.

findings.summary: Multiple zero-count public-context assignments are coverage NoData and could be misread as safe or absent.

findings.summary: Storm, coastal, heat/drought, winter, cyber, earthquake and omitted incident families are bounded exercises rather than calibrated Losser forecasts.
findings.evidence: The focused matrix is finite, but E03 supports high-sandy drought, forest/recreation, power/heating, cross-border and residual Emsland mechanisms that are not selected forcing. Coastal direct water is zero, canonical fire has zero local flame, earthquake has no local event/grid and cyber has no named target/architecture. Hazardous-material and radiological incidents are outside the ten presets.
findings.action: Keep scenario, observation, forecast, probability and official-warning labels distinct; require an explicit selected event/target and versioned forcing before local operational claims. Disclose omitted hazards rather than silently mapping them onto another preset.

findings.summary: The deterministic scenario contract, population/service reconciliation, causal arithmetic and selected-layer invariance pass for GM0168.
findings.evidence: The model gate passes two tests over every required preset, checkpoint and service. Zero-intensity outputs close exactly; all local populations and service demand/delivery totals reconcile within floating-point tolerance; repeated frames are deterministic; selected-layer local hazard delta is zero; cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic and route bounds hold.
findings.action: Retain these regressions while correcting named-river scope, spatial allocation, fire containment, cross-border networks, service semantics and action/provenance gaps. Mathematical closure is not local physical calibration.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning-model audit, not a KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat, Vechtstromen, Veiligheidsregio Twente, municipality, NLWKN, RIVM or infrastructure-operator forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration commitment.

The 2025 generalized CBS boundary and neighbourhoods support overview aggregation, not parcel hydraulics, cross-border catchments, terrain flow, forest fuel, asset ownership, incident perimeters or emergency routes.

No selected Dinkel/Glanerbeek rainfall or hydrograph, upstream/downstream boundary, gauge/datum, connected inundation footprint, control state, arrival/recession, verified depth unit, uncertainty or NoData mask drives GM0168.

The current nonzero Rhine/Meuse/IJssel direct result is unsupported locally; a future exact zero for that named scope cannot mean zero Dinkel, brook, pluvial, sewer, groundwater, access or indirect supply risk.
The Overijssel 70 mm/2 h layer is an official planning scenario, not current observation or T+72 forecast; it is not yet sampled by the model.
HWH objects are partial register geometry. They do not establish hydraulic connectivity, capacity, setpoint, operation, backup or restoration, and null fields remain Unknown.
Public grid-planning numbers are one postcode sample and not municipality coverage, live load, outage, topology, customer impact, reserve or restoration.

No complete public safe source provides electricity/gas feeders, Vitens pressure and water-quality topology, municipal sewer network, Vechtstromen control logic, telecom backhaul, facility dependencies, fuel/food stocks, backups, crews or restoration; sensitive facts were not inferred.
All eight services currently reuse six road-derived logical links. These are not physical utility, water, wastewater, telecom, patient-transfer or stocked-logistics networks.

NWB, ProRail and GTFS are static context; NDW is a deployment-time Dutch current picture. None establishes German continuity, incident-time passability, bridge state, evacuation throughput or future T+72 state.
RIVM hospital roles, room counts and visits do not establish ambulance time, reachability, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, diversion, generator/fuel or backup endurance.
RDI sites do not establish operator, coverage, traffic, power/backhaul, congestion, availability or restoration. DUO locations do not establish shelter, reception, care or distribution roles.

Current nature-fire phase 1 is not an ignition/fuel forecast or all-clear; the focused forest point is synthetic and no live moisture, wind, perimeter, suppression-water, access, evacuation or smoke-exposure model is calibrated.

Cyber has no named target, architecture or attack path; earthquake has no selected local event, ground-motion/site-response surface or fragility; residual Emsland/radiological and hazardous-material incidents are outside the ten presets.

Household preparedness, medically dependent people, visitors/workers, cross-border mutual aid, water/reception points, medicine, food/fuel, staff, vehicles and repair priorities remain assumptions or Unknown. Official 72-hour guidance is not measured readiness or an aid/recovery deadline.

Affected population is a current post-network people-equivalent threshold metric, while deprived person-hours is a cumulative local pre-network matched-baseline service-pressure proxy. Neither is identified customers, casualties, displacement, welfare loss or economic damage; six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid changes.
